stories.headline: Tamil Nadu Govt. to withdraw cases registered against students during anti-NEET protests
stories.deck: The Tamil Nadu government’s decision is in line with similar decisions taken by a few other State governments to withdraw cases registered against those who took part in protests against the NEET
stories.bodyText:
Minister for School Education Rajmohan on Sunday (August 2, 2026) said the Tamil Nadu government would withdraw all cases registered against students who protested against the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET).
In a post on X, Mr. Rajmohan said following the directions of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, all cases registered against students who protested against NEET would be withdrawn. He also said the government would announce further details shortly.
The announcement comes against the backdrop of nationwide protests against the NEET, last week. As thousands of students and youth staged a protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan (since resigned) and pressing a slew of other demands, protests were also held in Tamil Nadu. The demonstrations included flash protests at some places and a continuous protest at Balan Illam, the State headquarters of the Communist Party of India in Chennai.
At a few places, the police detained students who resorted to road blockades during the protests .
The Tamil Nadu government’s decision is in line with similar decisions taken by a few other State governments to withdraw cases registered against those who took part in protests against the NEET.
Published - August 02, 2026 12:15 pm IST

stories.headline: 'Drugs take families, careers to new low': PM Modi launches 'Nasha Mukt Yuva' campaign - top quotes
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday launched the 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan', calling on the country's youth to stay physically and mentally fit and remain away from drug abuse.
Here are the top quotes from his address:
Youth must stay fit for developed India
"Today, all countrymen have come together for a great and important resolve. The campaign we are witnessing is meant for individuals, families and society, but above all, it is for the nation. The campaign, 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat', clearly reflects this resolve. As the country moves towards the goal of a developed India, it is essential that our youth remain physically and mentally healthy and stay away from drugs and other such harmful substances."
"The campaign we are witnessing today is for the individual, the family, and society; above all, it is for the nation. The very name of this movement—the 'Drug-Free Youth' initiative under the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan — clarifies its resolve. As the nation sets its sights on becoming a Viksit Bharat, it is essential that our youth be healthy in body and mind, brimming with self-confidence, and forever free from the deadly habit of drugs. This is the objective of the campaign... This campaign was launched last year as a pilot project from Kashi... Over 125 spiritual organizations have joined us today for the welfare of crores of our fellow citizens."
"By being addiction-free, you need to protect your potential. You need to be aware that drugs get you high for a short time, but take your career and family to a new low/bottom.
From Varanasi to nationwide campaign
"As the MP from Kashi, I am happy that this campaign was launched last year from the sacred land of Kashi as a pilot project. Along with scientific clarity, it also carries spiritual energy. Social organisations and NGOs have joined this initiative for the welfare of crores of Indians. Together, they have prepared a roadmap through the Kashi Declaration. Today, we are witnessing how the welfare-oriented idea that emerged from Kashi has become a national project. From today, the Nasha Mukt Yuva campaign is being launched across the country."
"The 'Nasha Mukta Yuva Abhiyaan' is launching across the country today... There is immense power in collective action, and today, driven by that very strength, this campaign is set to touch the heart of every young person. Lakhs of youths across the nation took a pledge to stay free from drugs... The pledge taken today will continue to move forward steadily over the next hundred weeks."
Priyanshi Rastogi is a journalist with The Times of India. She primarily covers national and international news, along with business affairs. Her work focuses on the latest political events, in-depth explainers, features, offbeat articles and viral social media trending stories.

stories.headline: Kerala heavy rains LIVE: Eight dead, 13 injured, 8 missing following rains: Kerala CM
stories.deck: The Chief Minister also said that 27 houses were completely destroyed, 196 homes were partially damaged and 5,792 people have been shifted to the 209 relief camps set up across the State
stories.bodyText:
Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan today said that eight people have died, an equal number are missing and 13 were injured in the previous day’s heavy rains, which caused property damage, landslides and waterlogging in many parts of the State.
Also read | Cloudburst-like event exposes gaps in State’s weather forecasting, disaster preparedness
In a statement issued by his office, Mr. Satheesan also said that 27 houses were completely destroyed, 196 homes were partially damaged and 5,792 people have been shifted to the 209 relief camps set up across the state.
Meanwhile,Kerala braced for the likelihood of heavy rains and flooding on Sunday (August 2, 2026), the latest in a string of stormy days that have wreaked havoc across the State.
The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange alert for 12 districts. It has warned of heavy rains and the possibility of flash floods, mudslides, and road and neighbourhood inundation in Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Ernakulam, Idukki, Thrissur, Palakkad, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur, and Kasargod districts.

stories.headline: Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das | The three faces of a revolt
stories.deck: Fuelled by viral outrage and youthful anger, the Cockroach Janta Party’s rapid rise was driven by three very different men whose skills, ambitions and political histories transformed a satirical online campaign into a national protest that brought down Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan
stories.bodyText:
From satire to sit-in is the most popular, and perhaps the easiest, explanation for the student protest movement that culminated in the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. This explanation is empowering in its simplicity. But it is incomplete.
By now, everyone knows how the story goes. On May 15, 2026, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant likened unemployed youth turning to activism and social media to “cockroaches”, triggering widespread backlash. Seizing on the remark, Abhijeet Dipke, an Indian student in Boston, launched a satirical online platform for fellow “cockroaches”, transforming an insult into a rallying cry for disaffected youth. Within the first 24 hours, 50,000 people signed up. That number swelled to more than a million within five days, while the movement’s Instagram account surged past 22 million followers.
Yet behind the viral posts, soaring follower counts and colourful symbolism stood a trio: Abhijeet Dipke (30), Ashutosh Ranka (30) and Saurav Das (27), whose skills complemented one another. They come from different parts of the country, different social backgrounds and possess markedly different temperaments.
Those who have spent time around Jantar Mantar since the movement began describe Mr. Dipke as politically intuitive, though at times a touch emotional, and the beating heart of the movement. On July 18, after activist Sonam Wangchuk was removed from Jantar Mantar, it was Mr. Dipke who argued that the movement should escalate its demands. Instead of limiting itself to seeking Mr. Pradhan’s resignation, he proposed demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Mr. Dipke loves discussing A.R. Rahman’s music and reciting Shah Rukh Khan’s dialogues from Swades. He brought a sense of lightness to the protest, spending time in the evenings talking to the protesters, posing for pictures with them and cracking a joke every now and then.
Mr. Ranka, meanwhile, has been described as decisive, though at times authoritarian, and quicker to lose his temper than others. He remains the mind of the movement and its principal strategist. Mr. Das, the youngest of the three, is known as much for his affable demeanour as for his outreach skills, though colleagues say he can occasionally be indecisive.
If Mr. Ranka and Mr. Dipke rave about Shah Rukh Khan starrer Swades and Aamir Khan’s Rang De Basanti, Mr. Das represents the other end of the social spectrum where his favourite series is Modern Family — a mockumentary about a multigenerational family based out of Los Angeles.
Association with AAP
One obvious thread connecting the three is their association with the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), a link none of them has sought to conceal. Both Mr. Dipke and Mr. Ranka have worked for the party, while Mr. Das’s proximity to former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal is hardly a secret.
Mr. Dipke was born in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (formerly Aurangabad), Maharashtra, into a Dalit family, though his caste identity largely remained in the background during the protest. “He is a student leader who is also a Dalit and not the other way round,” a leader associated with the 36-day protest said. One occasion on which he publicly asserted his caste identity came after ink was thrown at him at Jantar Mantar on July 18. His response was brief: “Blue is my colour. Jai Bhim.”
He studied journalism at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth in Pune before moving to the U.S. in 2023 to pursue a Master’s degree in Public Relations at Boston University. Mr. Dipke worked in political communications and was associated with the AAP social media team between 2020 and 2023, working closely with senior leader Manish Sisodia.
Mr. Ranka’s journey to the CJP was unlike that of most protest leaders. Born and raised in Jaipur, he studied Materials Science and Engineering at IIT-Kanpur, where he was elected president of the Students’ Gymkhana, an early indication of his interest in public life.
He served as a Delhi Assembly Fellow during 2019-20, working closely with the team of former Delhi Chief Minister and current Leader of Opposition Atishi during the pandemic, before pursuing a Master’s in Public Administration at the London School of Economics. He subsequently worked with McKinsey & Company and with Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, before gradually moving away from the worlds of consulting and international policy in favour of Indian public life.
Mr. Ranka also worked on the AAP campaign for the February 2025 Delhi Assembly election, focusing exclusively on the New Delhi constituency, where Mr. Kejriwal was the candidate. He was part of the team examining voter deletions and continued to publicly defend Mr. Kejriwal and the party even after the election. His most recent article as AAP’s “national spokesperson” was published on March 16.
Unlike many political organisers, Mr. Ranka has never hidden his ambitions. He has often expressed a desire to focus on Rajasthan politics. Following the 2025 Assembly election, he turned his attention to the State, running campaigns to protect a 100-acre forest near Jaipur. More recently, he gave Rajasthan Education Minister Madan Dilawar a three-month ultimatum to address issues faced by students at Rajasthan University, warning that the CJP would otherwise seek the vice-chancellor’s resignation.
Saurav Das, the movement’s young spokesman, became its public face. A journalist before he became a protest leader, he understood how newsrooms functioned, how narratives were shaped and, more important, how to keep a movement in the headlines.
Mr. Das spent part of his childhood in Puducherry and speaks a smattering of Tamil. He studied Journalism and Mass Communication at Amity University, Noida, graduating in 2019. He is best known for his detailed profile of former Chief Justice of India D.Y. Chandrachud for The Caravan, and has also written for Frontline and other publications.
‘The language of Gen Z’
Mr. Das is also the co-founder of Climate Action Front, an initiative focused on climate governance, sustainability and environmental policy. Alongside journalism, he has been working on his debut book, Complicit Silence: The Court’s Role in India’s Quiet Suffering, which examines the judiciary’s role in contemporary India through a series of case studies involving citizens seeking justice. Videos of Mr. Das dancing after Mr. Pradhan’s resignation also went viral, attracting admiration as well as criticism. Mr. Das defended the celebrations as “the language of Gen Z”, arguing that young people express political victories differently.
None of the three had ever led a protest of this scale before they laid siege to the government near the 18th century observatory, Jantar Mantar. Nor had the majority of the protesters who took to the streets of Delhi, in response to their call. For now, the three insist that the CJP will continue to function as a pressure group rather than a political party.
Published - August 02, 2026 03:00 am IST

stories.headline: Students return to Jantar Mantar to debunk viral false protest videos
stories.deck: Student groups say social media posts falsely claiming fresh protests at Jantar Mantar prompted them to verify the claims with vendors and CCTV footage, and are planning to seek police action against the accounts.
stories.bodyText:
A week after the 36-day protest led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) ended at Jantar Mantar, students continue to return to the site, not to stage fresh demonstrations, but to counter what they describe as a wave of misleading social media posts falsely portraying the protest as ongoing.
Instagram has been flooded with videos claiming to show “live” scenes of students clashing with police and marching through heavy security at Jantar Mantar. Carrying timestamps including August 1, July 31 and July 30, several of the clips have amassed millions of views, fuelling speculation that the protest is continuing despite having officially concluded.
One video claiming to be a 6 a.m. update on August 1 has crossed 2.8 million views. Another, presented as a 6.30 a.m. update on July 31, has received 1.9 million views, while other similarly labelled clips have attracted tens of thousands of views.
The viral posts have prompted representatives of student organisations to visit the protest site, enquire with locals and even seek access to CCTV footage in an attempt to publicly refute what they call a fabricated narrative.
On Saturday (August 1) evening, the stretch from Patel Chowk Metro station to Jantar Mantar remained under heavy security. Personnel from the Delhi Police, Border Security Force (BSF) and Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) stood along the route, with police buses and patrol vehicles stationed every few metres. Workers were simultaneously repainting the yellow barricades erected outside the protest site, even as visitors and students continued to walk through the area.
“We have been seeing videos on Instagram claiming there are fresh protests by student unions at Jantar Mantar. We came here to verify and debunk those claims,” said Bhim Kumar, a representative of the Krantikari Yuva Sangathan (KYS).
“We spoke to local vendors, student organisations and media personnel, who confirmed no protests have taken place. Police officials have also termed these claims baseless. No student organisation has announced any protest after July 28, but these videos are misleading people into believing demonstrations are still continuing. They are also weakening our cause,” he said.
Student representatives said they also approached those handling CCTV cameras in the area to verify whether any gatherings had taken place. “So far we have not found any evidence to ascertain such protests. We will now discuss the issue with other student organisations before approaching the police with a formal complaint seeking action against the social media handles circulating the videos.
Other students also visited Jantar Mantar to coordinate legal assistance for protesters facing cases in different States and to review developments relating to FIRs registered during the agitation.
Mudita, who participated throughout the 36-day protest, said the movement had shifted from street demonstrations to outreach. “We are continuing to reach students across colleges and universities to discuss the larger problems in the education system. The protest was never only about seeking the Minister’s resignation, it was about addressing deeper structural issues. We are also working on concerns faced by student protesters, including FIRs registered in different States,” she said.
For traders around Jantar Mantar, however, the online misinformation has translated into quieter streets and lower sales. “People still believe the protest is continuing and are afraid to come here. Business has dropped sharply over the past week because visitors are staying away. For a Saturday, this is unusually quiet,” said Dharmender, who manages a 40-year-old sweet shop overlooking the protest site.
At a neighbouring juice stall, Sunny said business had been slowly recovering but remained below normal.“The situation became difficult after the protest. Students still come here every day, and office-goers have also started returning gradually,” he said.
An ice cream vendor outside the visitor entrance echoed the sentiment, saying the decline in footfall had significantly affected sales despite the hot weather.
Published - August 02, 2026 08:58 am IST

stories.headline: Karnataka Congress flags abusive post on Rahul
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A member of the Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) legal cell has lodged a complaint with cybercrime police, alleging that a defamatory 
Instagram
 video targeted Lok Sabha opposition leader 
Rahul Gandhi
.
According to the complaint filed by Siddaraju, some comments on the July 16 post contained obscene, sexually explicit and derogatory language targeting Rahul, while others included vulgar remarks that undermined the dignity of women.
Based on the complaint, the cyber crime police registered a case under relevant provisions of the Information Technology Act and Section 352 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of peace).
A senior police officer said efforts have been initiated to have the video removed from the platform, while further investigation is underway to trace the administrator of the Instagram account.

stories.headline: Shivakumar shortlists 20 MLAs for cabinet expansion
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
 has drawn up a shortlist of around 20 
Congress
 MLAs for the much-awaited cabinet expansion, with the final list expected to be cleared by the party high command Sunday night ahead of the likely swearing-in Monday.
Party insiders said 18-20 legislators could take the oath as ministers, depending on the high command’s final approval. The exercise is aimed at striking a balance between regions and communities while addressing growing aspirations within the ruling Congress. Several districts currently unrepresented in the cabinet are expected to get berths.
According to highly placed sources, the shortlisted names are: Ajay Dharam Singh (Kalaburagi), Yashavantharayagouda Patil (Vijayapura), Sharath Bachegowda (Bengaluru Rural), Rizwan Arshad (Bengaluru), AS Ponnanna (Kodagu), SS Mallikarjun (Davanagere), Laxman Savadi (Belagavi), Raghumurthy (Chitradurga), Annapoorna Tukaram (Ballari), a representative from Mysuru, Vijayanand Kashappanavar (Bagalkot), C Puttaranga Setty (Chamarajanagar), Rudrappa Lamani (Haveri), Anekal Shivanna (Bengaluru), N Cheluvarayaswamy (Mandya), Santosh Lad (Dharwad), KM Shivalingegowda (Hassan), Bangarpet Narayanaswamy (Kolar), Zameer Ahmed Khan (Bengaluru) and Laxmi Hebbalkar (Belagavi).
While the broad contours of the expansion have been worked out, the final composition will depend on last-minute consultations with the Congress high command. An official announcement is expected only after the approval comes through.

stories.headline: Karnataka govt builds anti-cheating wall for recruitment exams
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: With recruitment for 74,000 posts set to begin, the state govt has rolled out a multi-layered security system to make recruitment examinations leak-proof and transparent.
Home minister Priyank Kharge Saturday said the new safeguards include one-time lockable security trunks that trigger automatic alerts if opened without authorisation, five-layer tamper-proof packaging of question papers and high-security printing outside Karnataka.
In another first, jammers will be installed in every examination room instead of only at examination centres. Each candidate in the same hall will receive a different sequence of questions and answer options through complete randomisation, reducing the scope for copying.
To boost transparency, OMR sheets will be uploaded on the Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA) website within 24 hours of receipt, even before evaluation, allowing candidates to verify their answer sheets.
Examination centres will be sanitised 24 hours in advance, monitored through CCTV cameras and inspected by flying squads. Police and district authorities have been issued detailed standard operating procedures, while secure transport of question papers and OMR sheets has been put in place.
The govt will also monitor WhatsApp, Telegram, BitChat and Snapchat to detect rumours or question paper leaks. Surveillance has been stepped up on those accused in earlier exam scams, while coaching centres have been warned of strict action if they fail to report suspicious activities.
Candidates will be informed through admit cards about permitted and prohibited items. Those wearing religious symbols or attire will be allowed after mandatory frisking and have been advised to report to examination centres two-and-a-half hours before the test.
He appealed to candidates, parents and the media to report suspected malpractice through helpline 112 or the recruitment control room numbers 9480800308 and 9480800106.
Box
No ban on religious attire for police recruitment exam: Priyank
Home minister Priyank Kharge Saturday clarified that there is no ban on wearing religious attire during the police constable recruitment examination and urged candidates not to be misled by rumours. He said candidates wearing religious clothing will be allowed to take the exam after mandatory security and identity checks, provided they report to the examination centre two-and-a-half hours early. Kharge said hall tickets already specify permitted and prohibited items and asked candidates to follow the dress code.
-------
Measures to curb malpractices
-One-time lockable security trunks with automatic unauthorised-opening alerts and five-layer tamper-proof packaging of question papers
-Jammers to be installed in every examination room, instead of only at examination centres
-Examination centres to be sanitised 24 hours in advance, monitored through CCTV cameras and inspected by flying squads
-Govt to monitor messaging apps to detect rumours or question paper leaks

stories.headline: Now, Karnataka turns focus back to Mekedatu project, fresh DPR submission next week
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: With heavy rain in Kerala and Kodagu filling the Kabini and Harangi reservoirs and easing the immediate pressure over releasing Cauvery water to 
Tamil Nadu
, Karnataka govt has turned its focus back to the long-pending Mekedatu balancing reservoir project, chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
’s flagship initiative that he championed through a high-profile padayatra in 2022.
The state will submit a fresh detailed project report (DPR) to the Central Water Commission (CWC) next week after incorporating the technical corrections sought by the central agency, in another push to secure clearance for the Rs 9,000-crore project. Water resources minister Ramalinga Reddy told 
TOI
 that the revised DPR is ready and they would take it up for discussion either Monday or Tuesday and it will be submitted after addressing all the observations raised by CWC.
The renewed push comes as improved inflows to the Cauvery basin have given Karnataka some breathing space in the latest water-sharing dispute with Tamil Nadu. While an all-party meeting is expected to decide the state’s response to the Cauvery Water Management Authority’s (CWMA) direction to release water downstream, the govt is simultaneously pursuing what it sees as a long-term solution to recurring Cauvery disputes.
The proposed balancing reservoir, downstream of Krishnaraja Sagar (KRS) near the Karnataka-Tamil Nadu border, is intended to store surplus monsoon flows for regulated release while supplying drinking water to Bengaluru and neighbouring areas. Karnataka has consistently maintained that the project will not reduce Tamil Nadu’s share under the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal (CWDT) award but will improve river regulation during both surplus and distress years.
CWC recently returned Karnataka’s revised DPR after identifying deviations from the tribunal award and seeking fresh technical justification on key aspects of the project.
Among its objections, the commission pointed out that Karnataka had increased the proposed consumptive use of water from 4.7 tmcft in the 2019 DPR to 6.9 tmcft in the revised report submitted in April this year, exceeding the allocation permitted under the tribunal award. It also questioned the inclusion of the proposed Shivanasamudra run-of-river power project and a diversion weir, neither of which formed part of the original proposal. In addition, CWC sought revised calculations to justify the proposed 59.4 tmcft live storage capacity.
Officials said the fresh DPR would fully conform to the tribunal award and the Supreme Court’s 2018 judgment. The project has gained momentum after the Supreme Court recently clarified that Karnataka is free to construct a reservoir within its territory, subject to compliance with the Cauvery Tribunal award and statutory approvals. Shivakumar described it as a major legal victory for the state, adding that Parliament had also been informed of Karnataka’s legal right to build the balancing reservoir at the proposed site.
Drawing parallels with the recent agreement among Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana to build a balancing reservoir across the Tungabhadra under the leadership of Union water resources minister CR Patil, Shivakumar said interstate river disputes could be resolved through consensus while protecting the interests of all states.
Sources in the chief minister’s office said he is keen to facilitate a similar dialogue involving the chief ministers of Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry once the present tensions over Cauvery subside. “If the issue can be resolved through dialogue, let it be resolved that way. Let them receive what is rightfully theirs; we will never stand in the way. Likewise, we should secure the rights granted to us by the court,” Shivakumar said.
For Shivakumar, Mekedatu is as much a political commitment as an infrastructure project. He led a 172km padayatra from Sangama to Bengaluru in 2022 to mobilise public support for the project. With reservoir levels rising after widespread rain in the Cauvery catchment, the govt believes the immediate crisis has eased enough to renew its push for one of Karnataka’s most ambitious and politically significant water projects.
–
Photo: Mekedatu
Photo credit: File pic
Blurb
Mekedatu project has gained momentum after the Supreme Court recently clarified that Karnataka is free to construct a reservoir within its territory, subject to compliance with the Cauvery Tribunal award and statutory approvals

stories.headline: Build house within 5 years or lose your govt-allotted plot: Karnataka CM
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 The govt-allotted residential sites lying vacant across Karnataka could soon face scrutiny, with the govt warning that unused plots may be taken back if beneficiaries fail to build homes within the stipulated period.
Chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
 Saturday said beneficiaries of sites allotted by agencies such as the Bengaluru Development Authority (BDA), Karnataka Housing Board (KHB) and other govt bodies must construct at least a small house within five years.
Launching the GBA’s ‘Freedom from Waste’ campaign at Hebbal junction here, Shivakumar said vacant plots have increasingly become dumping grounds for construction debris and garbage, besides being misused for activities that tarnish Bengaluru’s image. “We can’t allow people to hold onto allotted sites vacant for years despite the availability of many financial schemes to take up construction. Many such plots are turning into dumping yards. At least a small house should come up within five years of allotment. They can always expand it later by demolishing the initial one. If no structure comes up within the stipulated period, they might have to pay double property tax or we can also take back the site,” CM said.
The CM clarified that the move applies only to sites allotted by govt agencies and not to privately owned lands. The announcement does not introduce a new rule. The five-year construction condition already forms part of the allotment terms of the BDA, KHB and other agencies. However, enforcement has so far been relatively lenient, with authorities generally imposing penalties, collecting additional charges or granting extensions based on individual circumstances instead of cancelling allotments.
Officials said agencies currently examine each case on its merits. Delays caused by pending approvals, financial difficulties and other genuine reasons are often considered before deciding whether to levy penalties or grant additional time. A BDA official said a significant number of allotted sites, particularly in layouts where roads, water supply and drainage infrastructure have already been provided, continue to remain vacant beyond the prescribed five-year period.
“Until now, we had the discretion to decide whether a penalty should be imposed or whether an allotment should be resumed based on the circumstances of each case. If the govt’s direction is implemented strictly, taking back vacant sites may become mandatory in several cases,” the official said.
Officials of the KHB said their existing practice is also to impose penalties on defaulters. However, if the govt’s proposed enforcement is formally notified, agencies may have to resume long-vacant sites instead of continuing with the current system of fines, notices and extensions.

stories.bodyText:
US President Donald Trump's family business Trump Organization has been accused by Capital One of having its bank accounts closed following an internal anti-money laundering (AML) review, according to a court filing amid ongoing legal battle.
In a court filing on Friday, the bank said the account closures were the result of "months of analysis and a careful review" conducted by its AML experts in line with internal policies and regulatory guidance and not politically motivated, as reported by Reuters.
"Documents and Plaintiffs' own allegations make clear that Capital One closed Plaintiffs' accounts for anti-money laundering ('AML') reasons," the filing said.
The accounts were held by the Trump Organization, the privately owned business conglomerate that oversees Trump's hotels, golf courses, real estate and other ventures. Large companies often operate hundreds of bank accounts across different entities and properties. US banks can close customer accounts after internal compliance and risk reviews if they determine the banking relationship no longer meets their anti-money laundering or regulatory standards.
Capital One did not directly accuse the Trump Organization of engaging in illegal money laundering. Instead, it argued that the decision was based on compliance and risk assessment procedures, not political considerations.
The filing marks the first time a bank has formally stated in court that anti-money laundering concerns were behind its decision to close the Trump Organization's accounts.
The bank is seeking dismissal of a lawsuit filed by the Trump Organization and Eric Trump in March 2025 in a Florida federal court. The lawsuit alleges that Capital One closed the accounts because of its "woke" beliefs and to align with the political climate following the January 6, 2021, attack on the US Capitol.
Capital One notified the Trump Organization in March 2021 that it would close more than 300 affiliated accounts.
The federal court in Miami has already dismissed two versions of the lawsuit while allowing the plaintiffs to amend their complaint. In Friday's filing, Capital One argued that the latest complaint "suffers from the same fundamental flaws" as the previous versions.
The bank described the allegations of political bias as "misguided" and said they were "based on cherry-picked quotations unsupported by the full context" of documents submitted to the court.
"The transaction patterns identified by Capital One are among the types of activity flagged by federal banking guidance," the filing said.
The dispute comes as the Trump administration has intensified scrutiny of alleged "debanking" by major financial institutions. Trump signed an executive order in August 2025 barring discriminatory debanking and, earlier this year, filed a separate lawsuit against JPMorgan Chase on similar grounds.
The Trump Organization and Eric Trump sued Capital One in March 2025, alleging the bank unlawfully closed more than 300 of their accounts in 2021 because of its "woke" beliefs and to align with the political climate following the January 6, 2021, attack on the US Capitol. They argued the closures amounted to discriminatory "debanking" and sought damages.

stories.headline: Passenger vehicle sales hit top gear as July dispatches jump 33%; Maruti, Hyundai set records
stories.deck: India's passenger vehicle sales saw robust growth in July. Leading manufacturers like Maruti Suzuki and Hyundai reported record monthly dispatches. Tata Motors and Mahindra & Mahindra also posted substantial increases in their sales. This strong momentum was supported by government demand-boosting measures. Automakers benefited from favorable economic conditions throughout the month.
stories.bodyText:
India's passenger vehicle industry is estimated to have posted one of its strongest monthly performances in July, with domestic dispatches rising by around 33% year-on-year to nearly 4.7 lakh units. Strong volumes from leading manufacturers, including 
Maruti Suzuki
 and Hyundai, along with robust growth reported by 
Tata Motors
 and Mahindra & Mahindra, helped drive the industry's expansion during the month.
The sustained momentum came as automakers continued to benefit from demand-supporting measures introduced over the past year, including GST 2.0, lower repo rates and income tax relief for individuals earning up to Rs 12 lakh.
"Industry (passenger vehicle sales) should be around 4.65 lakh to 4.7 lakh in July this year. In July last year, the industry was around 3.5 lakh, so it is almost a growth of 33%," Maruti Suzuki India Ltd (MSIL) senior executive officer, marketing & sales, Partho Banerjee, told reporters in a conference call.
Explaining the factors supporting the market, Banerjee said GST 2.0, repo rate cuts and income tax relief for entry-level customers had continued to boost demand since last year.
"Fundamentally, these three tailwinds are very much there," Banerjee noted.
Maruti and Hyundai set new records
Maruti Suzuki led the market with its highest-ever domestic passenger vehicle sales of 1,96,203 units in July, compared with 1,37,776 units in the same month last year, registering a growth of 43.4%. "The company has witnessed all-round growth across segments from entry-level small cars to SUVs in July," Banerjee said, adding that alternate fuel CNG models continue to have robust demand.
Hyundai Motor India Ltd (HMIL) achieved its best-ever domestic monthly sales since inception, dispatching 54,210 units in July, up 23.3% from a year ago. "Our highest-ever monthly volume since inception, underscores the immense trust consumers place in brand Hyundai," HMIL MD & CEO Tarun Garg said.
Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd (TMPVL) also reported one of the steepest gains among major carmakers, with domestic passenger vehicle sales jumping 58% to 62,611 units in July from 39,521 units in the corresponding month last year.
Mahindra & Mahindra followed the suit, posting healthy growth, with domestic utility vehicle sales rising 20% to 60,048 units from 49,871 units a year earlier.
At the same time, Honda Cars India Ltd (HCIL) recorded domestic sales of 6,014 units during the month, reflecting growth of more than 48% over July last year.
Momentum remains strong
Apart from Indian auto giants, global car manufacturers also registered strong growth. Toyota Kirloskar Motor posted domestic sales of 30,516 units in July, up 5% from 29,159 units in the same month of 2025.
Kia India registered wholesale dispatches of 28,200 units, marking a 27.4% increase over 22,135 units a year ago. The company said it was its best-ever July wholesale performance since inception.
JSW MG Motor India also reported its highest-ever monthly wholesale volumes, dispatching 8,158 units to dealers during the month, up 22% year-on-year.
Nissan Motor India Pvt Ltd (NMIPL) more than tripled its domestic wholesale volumes, reporting 4,518 units in July compared with 1,420 units in the same month last year.

stories.headline: Zepto to raise funds amid delayed listing
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Zepto on Saturday said that it will raise funds through a pre-IPO financing amid tepid response from investors to its public listing.
Zepto did not share the specifics of the transaction but said that the move will strengthen its balance sheet. It is looking to raise around Rs 1,000 crore through the round at a valuation of $4-4.5 billion, sharply lower than its last valuation of $7 billion, TOI had reported.
On Friday, co-founder & CEO Aadit Palicha had told employees that the company will defer its IPO by two to three quarters. The startup which was initially eyeing a listing around July has stalled the process after domestic investors valued it at $3-3.5 billion.

stories.headline: 5.9 crore returns filed till July 31 deadline: I-T dept
stories.deck: Nearly 5.9 crore income tax returns were filed by the July 31 deadline. This number is lower than last year's extended filing period. Major tax concessions were announced during the last financial year. Taxpayers can still file returns until December with a penalty. Business income filers have different extended deadlines for their submissions.
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The I-T department on Saturday said that 5.9 crore returns had been filed till July 31, the deadline for most individuals to make their annual filing.
The number is lower than the over 7.3 crore returns that were filed by Sept 16, 2025, which was the extended deadline for filing last year. The numbers are likely to be lower as govt had announced major tax concessions during the last financial year, with income up to Rs 12 lakh.
According to official data, including revised returns, 8.7 crore returns were filed by individuals in FY2024-25, with a little less than 8.1 crore return filers in the segment.
“Your trust and timely compliance provide the energy that fuels India’s growth,” the Central Board of Direct Taxes said in a post on X. Those who have missed the deadline can still file returns till Dec but will have to shell out a penalty.
Taxpayers who have business income and have to use ITR-3 can file returns up to Aug 31, while those using ITR-4 regime can file returns up to Oct 31.
The I-T department’s numbers indicate returns were staggered over a period with no last-minute rush. Till late Friday morning, 5.5 crore returns had been filed with 42 lakh on Wednesday.

stories.headline: UPI transactions touch Rs 76cr/day, FASTag declines
stories.deck: UPI processed 2,366 crore transactions in July, showing significant year-on-year growth. NETC FASTag transactions declined by 6% compared to the previous year. The value of UPI transactions rose to Rs 29.88 lakh crore in July. NETC FASTag transaction value also saw a decrease from the prior month. UPI handled an average of 76.3 crore transactions daily in July.
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: UPI transactions scaled new highs in July 2026, while NETC FASTag transactions declined on a year-on-year basis. UPI processed 2,366 crore transactions in July, up 4.1% from 2,272 crore in June. On a year-on-year basis, transaction count grew 22%. In contrast, NETC FASTag processed 34.7 crore transactions in July, down 4.1% from 36.2 crore in June and 6% a year earlier.
The value of UPI transactions rose to Rs 29.88 lakh crore in July from Rs 28.92 lakh crore in June, an increase of 3.3%, but it was marginally below the Rs 29.9 lakh crore recorded in May. 
UPI handled an average of 76.3 crore transactions in July daily, up from 75.7 crore in June. The average daily transaction value stood at Rs 96,383 crore, almost unchanged from Rs 96,405 crore in June. 
The value of NETC FASTag transactions stood at Rs 7,143 crore in July, down 1% from Rs 7,215 crore in June. It was also lower than the Rs 7,308 crorein May. TNN

stories.headline: Young Indian shuttler Tanvi Sharma wins maiden BWF Super 300 title at Taipei Open
stories.deck: The 17-year-old from Punjab, who had finished runner-up at last year's U.S. Open Super 300, needed just 36 minutes to outclass Nguyen in the summit clash
stories.bodyText:
Teen Indian sensation Tanvi Sharma won her maiden BWF World Tour title after defeating Vietnam's sixth seed Thuy Linh Nguyen 21-16 21-16 in the women's singles final of the Taipei Open Super 300 badminton tournament in Taipei on Sunday (August 2, 2026).
The 17-year-old from Punjab, who had finished runner-up at last year's U.S. Open Super 300, needed just 36 minutes to outclass Nguyen in the summit clash.
Coached by P.V. Sindhu's former mentor Park Tae-sang, Tanvi also became the first Indian to win the women's singles title at the Taipei Open since Saina Nehwal, who had lifted the trophy in 2008.
Tanvi made a flying start, repeatedly catching Nguyen at the front court with deft drops played with the same action as a smash to open up a 4-1 lead. The Vietnamese struggled to read the Indian's deception and also found it difficult to judge the drift, going wide twice as Tanvi mixed steep cross-court smashes with her trademark touch to surge to a 10-2 advantage.
The Indian, however, suddenly slipped into a string of errors, struggling to keep the shuttle inside the lines. She eventually produced a timely smash to carry a three-point lead into the mid-game interval, with coach Park Tae-sang urging her to relax.
Tanvi found her rhythm after the break, producing powerful smashes from both flanks to move 15-9 ahead. Though she gifted away a few points with errors at the net and from the back court, she regained control, earning five game points before sealing the opening game with a cross-court smash.
After the change of ends, Nguyen opened a 3-0 lead by making Tanvi cover the court with sharp angles. But the Indian slowly began dictating the rallies, drawing level at 3-3 with a fine net shot before once again pushing her opponent deep and catching her at the net with deft touches.
Nguyen's inconsistency also helped Tanvi build an 8-4 lead before another patch of errors allowed the Vietnamese to close the gap to 7-8, prompting Park to tap his head in frustration. Two exquisite deceptive winners helped Tanvi take an 11-8 lead at the interval.
The Indian gradually stretched the advantage to 15-10 and then 18-12, her deception once again fetching crucial points. At 19-12, Tanvi unsuccessfully challenged a line call after being ruled late, but soon earned seven match points with a smash. A nervous finish saw her squander three of them before she finally converted to seal her maiden BWF title.
In a heartwarming moment, Tanvi took off her gold medal and placed it around coach Park Tae-sang's neck before the two posed together for photographs.
At 17 years and 222 days, Tanvi is the youngest finalist in the tournament's history, surpassing Korean doubles great Lee Yong Dae, who was 17 years and 287 days old when he reached the men's doubles final in 2006.
Tanvi had become the first Indian to win two medals at a single edition of the World Junior Championships, securing silver in girls' singles and bronze in the mixed team event. She was also a member of the Indian team that won the country's maiden gold medal at the Asian Team Championships.
A former world junior No. 1, Tanvi reached her maiden Super 300 final at the 2025 US Open at the age of 16. She also finished runner-up at the Odisha Masters Super 100 and Guwahati Masters Super 100.
Published - August 02, 2026 11:47 am IST

stories.headline: Messi returns as Inter Miami draw 2-2 against Columbus Crew
stories.deck: The result ended Miami's six-match winning streak and kept them in second place in the Eastern Conference behind Nashville, who drew 2-2 at DC United
stories.bodyText:
Lionel Messi returned to Major League Soccer action after World Cup duty on Saturday (August 1, 2026), coming on in the second half as his Inter Miami side drew 2-2 with Columbus Crew.
Two weeks after Argentina's loss to Spain in the World Cup final, Messi was back on the pitch, entering in the 53rd minute to the delight of fans at Miami's Nu Stadium.
But Messi could not mark his return with a goal, twice shooting wide.
Uruguayan Luis Suarez scored his seventh goal in his last four games to put Miami 1-0 up in the 16th minute.
Miami's former Manchester United and Real Madrid midfielder Casemiro scored an own goal in the 34th minute, which drew Columbus level at 1-1.
Suarez provided the assist for Noah Allen to head Miami into a 2-1 half-time lead
But midfielder Brais Mendez, making his Columbus debut after arriving from Real Sociedad in Spain, curled in a second equalizer from an 84th-minute free-kick.
The result ended Miami's six-match winning streak and kept them in second place in the Eastern Conference behind Nashville, who drew 2-2 at DC United.
Los Angeles FC and Vancouver Whitecaps remain level at the top of the Western Conference after they drew 1-1 at Vancouver's BC Place.
Son Heung-min extended his scoring streak since the MLS resumed after the World Cup to four goals in four matches as he put Los Angeles ahead in the 37th minute.
But Vancouver's German star Thomas Mueller converted a 76th-minute penalty.
The former Tottenham star Son, who had shouldered much of the blame for South Korea's failure to make it to the knockout rounds of the World Cup, also earned MVP honors in the MLS All-Star Game on Wednesday.
Published - August 02, 2026 11:20 am IST

stories.headline: Fleming a 'big reason' for Root's return as England captain
stories.deck: Root replaced Ben Stokes ‌after the all-rounder retired following the home series ​against New Zealand
stories.bodyText:
Joe Root said Stephen Fleming's appointment as England's test coach was a "big reason" he agreed to return as captain of the squad.
Root replaced Ben Stokes after the all-rounder retired following the home series against New Zealand. Fleming succeeds compatriot Brendon McCullum, whose four-year test tenure ended last month, though he remains England's white-ball coach.
"If I'm being brutally honest, it was a big reason why I wanted to do it," Root told the England and Wales Cricket Board.
"I'm very excited by the way he sees the game, where he sees us sit as a team, and the work that we have to do to get to where we want to get to. All of that got me very excited about taking this role on."
"He's obviously got a wealth of experience and done some amazing things within the game as a player and as a coach, and I'm very much looking forward to the next little while, and us trying to build something pretty special together."
Former New Zealand captain Fleming coached Chennai Super Kings for 17 years in the Indian Premier League before leaving last month. Root led England as their full-time test captain between 2017 and 2022 before he was replaced by Stokes. Stokes and McCullum championed a take-no-prisoners approach, which endeared them to the fans and Root hinted he and Fleming would like to retain that attacking mindset. "The last four years have been the most fun I've had in professional cricket...," said the 35-year-old.
"Clearly, the last little while is probably what's fresh in everyone's mind, but you're looking at a four-year period where we did a lot of amazing things. "I've taken a lot from that, and I feel it will be a big part of how I want to approach things moving forward as a leader of this team." England host Pakistan for a three-test series beginning in Leeds on August 19.
Published - August 02, 2026 10:51 am IST

stories.headline: 'We're very aligned': Joe Root reveals why Fleming won him over instantly
stories.deck: Joe Root expressed enthusiasm for leading England's Test team again. He cited incoming coach Stephen Fleming as a key reason for his excitement. Fleming's vision has Root looking forward to the team's future prospects. Root also acknowledged the positive impact of Brendon McCullum and Ben Stokes. England's next assignment is a home series against Pakistan in August.
stories.bodyText:
Joe Root
 has hailed incoming England Test coach 
Stephen Fleming
 as a major reason behind his enthusiasm for leading the side again, saying the former New Zealand captain's vision has left him excited about the team's future.
England confirmed Fleming as their new Test coach earlier this week after parting ways with 
Brendon McCullum
 last month. The 53-year-old will officially begin his tenure later this year.
Root returned as England captain during the second Test against New Zealand in June after Ben Stokes was removed from the role following a nightclub brawl incident after the series opener. Although Stokes was later cleared and returned to play his final Test, Root retained the captaincy, marking his second stint as England's Test skipper.
Speaking about his first interactions with Fleming, Root said the conversations immediately convinced him that the pair shared a similar outlook.
"I've admired him from afar, first as a player and recently as a coach. To get the chance to work together is going to be great fun. Once I'd spoken to Stephen about it and saw his energy and excitement for it, and saw we're very aligned on it, I got excited very quickly. Hopefully, we can work and build on a lot of the good things that have happened over the last four years," Root told BBC Sport.
Root also paid tribute to McCullum and Stokes, crediting the former leadership duo for transforming England's Test setup and changing his own perspective on the game.
"I think Brendon and Ben did a brilliant job, in many ways, of turning things around and getting us in a position where hopefully now we can carry that forward in a slightly different way. Hopefully, we can work and build on a lot of the good things that have happened over the last four years.
"The last four years have been the most fun I've had in professional cricket, and a big part of that was down to the way they [McCullum and Stokes] got me to see the game.
"Clearly, the last little while is probably what's fresh in everyone's mind, but you're looking at a four-year period where we did a lot of amazing things. I've taken a lot from that, and I feel it will be a big part of how I want to approach things moving forward as a leader of this team,” he added.
England's next Test assignment is a three-match home series against Pakistan, beginning on August 19 at Headingley. Fleming, however, will not take charge for that series. Assistant coach Marcus Trescothick will oversee the team before Fleming officially starts his tenure during England's series against South Africa in December.

stories.headline: 'Questions will be asked': Ex-India star's message for Gambhir
stories.deck: Former India wicketkeeper Deep Dasgupta anticipates pressure on coach Gautam Gambhir and captain Shubman Gill. India has lost recent Test series, and this Sri Lanka tour is crucial. The team needs to show clear direction during this transition period. Winning seven out of nine remaining Tests is vital for WTC final hopes. Dasgupta stressed that no Test series can be taken lightly by India.
stories.bodyText:
Former India wicketkeeper-batter Deep Dasgupta believes head coach 
Gautam Gambhir
 will be under pressure when India begin their two-match Test series against Sri Lanka in Galle on August 15. India have lost Test series against New Zealand, Australia and South Africa under Gambhir, and will now look to bounce back against Sri Lanka.
Dasgupta said the pressure will not only be on Gambhir but also on captain 
Shubman Gill
 and the rest of the Indian team.
"As we are saying, two out of three series have been lost. So, there will be pressure. It is also important to say that all the names we are taking, everyone knows how to play under pressure, and they also know how to handle it. But there will be pressure on Shubman, the Indian players, and it is very, very important," Deep Dasgupta told IANS
WTC Standings
"Because they are talking about transition, it is very important to see a direction in the transition period. The transition started, let's say, after the New Zealand Test series; then came the England series and all of that. It started from there onwards. Somewhere, I feel that it is important to see a direction, and I am a little confused as to which direction we are going," he concluded.
Dasgupta added that questions are bound to be asked if India's struggles continue.
"One thing is fair: questions will be asked of him (Gambhir). 
When the team does not play properly, questions will be asked individually. Obviously, the team's coach, captain, and everyone involved with the team will be asked questions because, if you look at it, we lost at home. After 2011-12, we lost the series in New Zealand, and we kept losing continuously," Deep Dasgupta said.
India's chances of reaching the WTC final
Dasgupta also warned that India cannot afford to take any opposition lightly, especially with difficult away assignments coming up. 
The Sri Lanka series could play a key role in India's hopes of reaching the World Test Championship (WTC) final. 
India have nine Tests left in the current WTC cycle - away series in Sri Lanka - 2 Tests, away series against New Zealand - 2 Tests, home series against Australia - 5 Tests).
India tour of Sri Lanka: Full schedule
"Well, firstly, there is no easy Test series, and especially right now, looking at the Indian Test side, which is going through a transition, there is not one easy Test match, no matter what happens."
"Especially in Sri Lanka. Again, Sri Lanka has been a very difficult place to tour in the past, especially in these conditions right now. So, I think it's going to be interesting when looking at the WTC. I think there are nine Test matches left: five against Australia, two against Sri Lanka, and two against New Zealand. If I'm not wrong, roughly speaking, I think seven out of nine will have to be won to qualify for the WTC final.
 So, that in itself is a difficult task."
"On top of that, you have Sri Lanka in Sri Lanka and New Zealand in New Zealand. These are difficult assignments. On top of that, if we look at it series by series, and if we don't count Afghanistan's one-off Test, then in the last three series, we have lost two, against New Zealand and South Africa. So, that is one thing. Obviously, that's why you can't take any series or opposition lightly at this time, in any condition," he said.

briefs.headline: CWG 2026: India’s medal-heavy day delivers seven boxing golds
briefs.deck: India enjoyed its best day of the 2026 Commonwealth Games, winning 16 medals to climb to fourth in the standings with 39 medals overall. A historic boxing campaign delivered seven golds and three silvers, while athletics, para athletics and judo added six more medals. India also reached the mixed 4x400m relay final and remained in contention for more success on the final day.
